KIDFLUENCERS [6221]

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The child influencer is on the rise, and they are a dream come true for brands trying to sell things to children

Unique Selling Point:
The child influencer is on the rise, and they are a dream come true for brands trying to sell things to children
If you tune into these kidfluencers accounts, they are all super cute kids bringing you content about their fabulous lives. Content that seems to largely be curated by their parents.
But these kids they aren’t just being cute, they are promoting toys, tv shows, clothes, basically anything kids can buy, they are marketing. They are making big money from big brands, and for big brands. It’s like the Hight of capitalism, commercializing childhood.

We go behind the scenes, into the lives of some of South Africa’s biggest Kidfluencers, speaking to them and their parents, we also speak to a digital anthropologist, social media legal expert and a Child Psychologist to unpack this industry, how it is being regulated and what are the potential long-term side-effects for these children.




Summary:
But their parents would argue that their kids are the ones wanting to make the videos and they have fun doing, also no-one is getting hurt. A lot of these Kidfluencers are also the offspring of Influencers or famous parents, so they are already part of the industry as such.

But it’s a controversial topic with one specialist in a New York Times article calling it the modern “digital child labor”
At large its classic momanger setup, mom dad is often off screen directing the cuteness, telling them what to say or asking questions to guide the content. But why would a parent put their child on social media for millions to watch, comment and own. Is it because they are proud of them or is it to make money? And if it’s about money, whose money is it, as the child is the influencer, but the parent creates the content?

Consent is another grey area in this culture, a child can’t really consent to their person being put on social media for millions to see, as they can’t grasp the magnitude of having everything they do magnified or the concept of a digital footprint. One day, when they are old enough, if they decide they no longer want to be a kidfluencer, it’s too late because they’ve gone viral

Another social media specialist also pointed that the internet is a dark world and when you as a parent think you are posting a beautiful video of your child, that image can be used in the most grotesque way by pedophiles around the world. Instagram has also become a marketplace for child trafficking, where a child can be sold before they are even abducted.


Further information:
Sbahle Mzizi - 5 years old
Instagram - 1M followers
Youtube - 65k + subscribers TICK TOCK 13.8KFollowers 16.8KLikes


Sbahle is the child of actress and TV presenter Ntando Duma and DJ Junior De Rocka. She first came onto the internet as a meme and would have a word of the day with their meanings. At the age of three-year-old, she made her runway debut in October 2019 at the AFI (African Fashion International) Joburg Fashion Week. She is the brand ambassador of a number of brands like Disney Africa, Game stores and Omo berry. She also has a YouTube channel with over 38 000 subscribers with close to 1 million views.

Taylor Morrison - 7 years old
Instagram - 117k Followers
Facebook - 200 000 + followers
Youtube - 2.35k subscribers

Sassy Taylor Morrison is South Africa’s sweetheart who was discovered at the age of 2 years old when her mother posted a video of her holding her cousin. Taylor has been a social media influencer and has gained traction on Instagram, Facebook and TikTok and has attracted more than 340 000 followers across these platforms with her cute, kid-friendly content. Her content sees Taylor unpacking and reviewing products such as Barbie, Fashion Nova, Rookie USA, top toys, and Cotton on to name a few.
